title: Researching any tech node (or capturing any sector) free-unlocks the objective-free early tech tree

path.to: Campaign -> Serpulo -> Ground Zero -> research the Mechanical Drill -> reopen the Tech Tree

java: gradlew desktop:run; fresh profile; play groundZero; research mechanicalDrill; open the tech tree
only mechanicalDrill (+ already-unlocked/zero-requirement nodes) is unlocked; conveyor/junction/mechanical-pump still require their copper research
godot: launch Serpulo/Ground Zero on a fresh profile; research mechanical-drill; reopen the tech tree

conveyor, junction, router, distributor, sorter, item-bridge, core-foundation, core-nucleus, mechanical-pump, conduit chain, graphite-press, laser-drill, ... are already unlocked and their costs were never paid
compare: diff the unlocked node set after the first research; upstream unlocks only zero-requirement objective-free nodes, the port unlocks the whole objective-free subtree reachable from the root

plan.state: seeded by code-scan 2026-10-10; not yet verified in-engine

plan.approach: 1) Materialize `content_research_requirements()` (and the multiplier scaling already used by `effective_requirements`) into `TechNode.requirements`/`finished_requirements` when `at_full_inner` gets no explicit list, mirroring `TechTree.node(content, children)` -> `content.researchRequirements()` (TechTree.java:31-33/167-175); keep ids/order untouched but re-record affected campaign goldens and `CHECKSUM_VERSION`-adjacent outputs if the stored lists change observable dumps. 2) Also insert the upstream `Research(dependency)` objectives from `content.getDependencies()` so node gating matches, or make `check_auto_unlocks` consult `effective_requirements()` instead of the stored list. 3) Add the regression scenario: after a research/capture sweep, `conveyor` must still be locked and `mechanical-drill` must require its real copper cost.

Upstream checkAutoUnlocks tests node.requirements.length == 0 against the list materialized from content.researchRequirements() at node build; the port's generated trees leave requirements empty (TechTreeBuilder::at_full_inner sets Vec::new() when no explicit list, mod.rs:306-316) and check_auto_unlocks tests that stored list (tech_tree.rs:344), so any research that unlocks something (campaign.rs:931-938) or any sector capture (campaign.rs:447-461) sweeps and unlocks every not-yet-unlocked node whose parent chain is unlocked and whose objectives are complete, free of cost. title: Campaign sector progression is forgotten after a client restart (captures, attempts, stored items, import/export routes reset)

path.to: Campaign -> capture a sector -> save & quit -> relaunch the client -> planet page sector panel

java: gradlew desktop:run; capture frozenForest; quit; relaunch
the planet page still shows the sector captured with its attempt count, stored items and (for legacy bases) import/export destination
godot: capture any sector; quit to the menu and restart the client; reopen the planet page

was_captured/attempts/items/production/origin/destination are back to defaults; the next campaign turn's production pass writes those defaults over the stored `<planet>-s-<id>-info` JSON (universe.rs:653)
compare: compare the sector record (`<planet>-s-<id>-info`) and the panel rows before/after a relaunch

plan.state: seeded by code-scan 2026-10-10; not yet verified in-engine
plan.seam: game::universe::Campaign::load_all / MindCampaign::bootstrap never call SectorInfoState::load_info, and the resume path never applies SectorInfoState::write (upstream Planet.init -> sector.loadInfo and Logic SaveLoadEvent -> info.write)
plan.approach: 1) In `Campaign::load_all` (after `planet.load_rules`/`load_stats`) iterate planets/sectors and call `sector.load_info(settings, &planet.name)` so `was_captured`/`attempts`/items/production/waves/origin/destination survive restarts (Planet.java:459-463). 2) On `play_sector` (and the host resume path), apply the stored record to the session before `RulesLoad`: wave/winWave/waves/attack plus the stored item pool written into the player core (`SectorInfo.write`, upstream Logic.java:78-86). 3) Ensure the production-pass `save_info` (universe.rs:653) only runs after the load, so it stops clobbering the stored JSON with defaults.
plan.narrow_check: cargo test -p mind-core game && the headless round-trip already sketched in mind-headless campaign_scenarios.rs:414-420 (save_info -> rebuild -> load_info asserts the record survives)

note: Code-scan 2026-10-10 (campaign): S2/high. `SectorInfoState::load_info` has no non-test caller; `Campaign::load_all` loads only planet rules/stats and universe counters (universe.rs:732-738), and `MindCampaign::bootstrap` only re-derives `sector.save` from files (campaign.rs:199-206). `SectorInfoState::write` (the resume-time apply, sector.rs:369) is also uncalled. The production pass then calls `save_info` on the default-initialized record (universe.rs:653), overwriting the stored JSON. Player impact: after any restart the campaign forgets which sectors were captured, their attempts/wave/item pools and their inter-sector routes; `initial` capture bookkeeping (stats/last-sector victory) can re-fire. Related but distinct from PAR-0037 (Ground Zero world round-trip, verified). In-engine verification pending.

plan.seam: the live campaign never feeds or refreshes SectorInfo: no caller of SectorInfoState::update/prepare/write and CoreCampaignHooks defaults to a no-op, so the production_pass/export_import_pass maps stay empty
plan.approach: 1) Implement `CoreCampaignHooks` over the live `CampaignRuntime` so core item deltas reach the played sector's `handle_core_item`/`handle_production` (upstream CoreBlock.java:794/808/881/895); wire LaunchPad/LandingPad import/export when those blocks land. 2) In `campaign_tick_system` or a new `TickSet::Campaign` system, call `sector.info.update(1/60, item_index_of)` for the played sector each tick (Logic.java:538) and flush on the autosave cadence. 3) At the save boundary (`SimIoHandler::save` / `live_meta_tags`), build a `CoreSnapshot` from the world and call `SectorInfoState::prepare` + `save_info` (SaveVersion.java:116-118).
plan.narrow_check: cargo test -p mind-core world::blocks::storage + a headless scenario that runs a core-fed production line for N ticks, then asserts the sector's production window/items are non-zero and survive a save/load

note: Code-scan 2026-10-10 (campaign): S2/high. `SectorInfoState::update` (sector.rs:324) and `prepare` (sector.rs:334) have zero non-test callers; the only `CoreCampaignHooks` impl is a test `Incinerating` (core_block.rs:442-455) so `handle_core_item` never records live deltas; `SimIoHandler`'s live meta write (sim_io.rs:264-299) never runs `prepare`/`saveInfo`. `Campaign::run_turn`'s production/import passes (universe.rs:588-656) read `info.production`/`info.export`, which therefore stay empty: offline production and legacy-pad imports/exports are dead, and the planet panel's production/export/import/stored rows never populate. title: Losing a sector and re-attacking it restores your base instead of applying the loss damage

path.to: Campaign -> Serpulo -> lose a sector (core destroyed while attacked) -> planet page -> re-launch the sector

java: build a defended base in a Serpulo sector, let the core fall, return to the planet page and re-launch
most defenses are destroyed by SectorDamage(1f), the base is rebuilt from the saved plans; the match resumes from the sector record
godot: same steps in the port: the launch takes the resume branch (play_sector.rs:415-431 sees the stale has_core=true) and loads the last save as-is
maps::sector_damage::apply has no live caller, so no simulated loss damage and no plan-based restore happen
compare: count surviving turrets/blocks after re-launching a lost sector in both clients

plan.state: seeded by code-scan 2026-10-10; not yet verified in-engine
plan.seam: game::play::play_sector branch selection (has_core from the never-refreshed sector record) and the missing mind-core::maps::sector_damage::apply call in the lost-sector replay path
plan.approach: 1) Decide `hasBase` like upstream: after the host loads the save, treat the sector as lost when the loaded world has no default-team cores (or the record's prepared has_core is false), not from the stale in-memory boolean (Control.java:456/465). 2) On that branch re-place the planet's default core at `sector.info.spawn_position`, run `maps::sector_damage::apply(tiles, content, state, 1.0, rng, fx)` to destroy most defenses (Control.java:482), then restore the previously captured plans/buildings (upstream keeps `previousPlans`/`previousBuildings` and replays them onto the fresh world). 3) Keep Erekir `clearSectorOnLose=true` behavior unchanged.
plan.narrow_check: headless scenario: build + save a sector, remove the player core, replay via play_sector, assert the surviving building count dropped and the prior plans are present; cargo test -p mind-core maps::sector_damage

note: Code-scan 2026-10-10 (campaign): S2/medium. play_sector's own comment says the damaged-core re-derivation is deferred and 'the sector is relaunched fresh, matching upstream's hadNoCore fallback' (play.rs:400-403), but the code only relaunches when `!has_save || !has_core`; has_core is set true at launch (campaign.rs:593) and never refreshed (the sibling sector-info load/prepare gaps), so a lost Serpulo sector (clearSectorOnLose=false) resumes the last save unchanged. `maps::sector_damage::apply` (sector_damage.rs:92) is called only from tests. Player impact: re-attacking a lost sector starts from the intact saved base rather than upstream's damaged base + rebuild plans; the base-less resume also has no core/plan restore. Related existing item: PAR-0040 covers the Abandon flow, not the loss/damage simulation. In-engine verification pending.
